TF-020H3rg-002 in STATUS.md explicitly acknowledges the missing hash-pinning gap. Blast radius: arbitrary issue creation on SCP repo + read-only checkout content access. No contents:write, no push, no secret exfiltration beyond GH_TOKEN itself. findings.claim: issues:write is granted at the job level, meaning every step in the release-gate job — including the unverified pyyaml/jsonschema pip-install and the Python evaluation steps — runs with an issues:write-capable GITHUB_TOKEN in scope. A supply-chain compromise of either pinned-but-not-hash-verified package (TF-020H3rg-002) would give attacker-controlled code running in those earlier steps the ability to create arbitrary issues on the SCP repo using the ambient GH_TOKEN.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml:63-70 — permissions block sets issues:write at the job (not step) level; GitHub Actions does not support step-level permission scoping. release-gate.yml:101-111 — pip install --quiet --user 'pyyaml==6.0.2' 'jsonschema==4.23.0' with no --require-hashes; this step runs before the issue-opening step with issues:write in scope. TF-020H3rg-002 in STATUS.md explicitly acknowledges the missing hash-pinning gap. Pre-020H.3.1, the workflow held only contents:read (release-gate.yml had no issues:write before this slice), so this slice is the introduction point for the elevated privilege. The canary-replay.yml parallel (which already had issues:write) has the same pattern but was outside prior release-gate review scope.
findings.impact: Two-step exploit chain: (1) a PyPI supply-chain compromise of pyyaml 6.0.2 or jsonschema 4.23.0 (both version-pinned without hash verification), AND (2) the attacker-injected code uses the ambient GH_TOKEN (which has issues:write + contents:read per the job-level permissions block) to open arbitrary issues on the SCP repo. Blast radius: arbitrary issue creation on SCP repo + read-only checkout content access. No contents:write, no push, no secret exfiltration beyond GH_TOKEN itself. The risk is amplified rather than created by TF-020H3rg-002 remaining open — the open tracking item now has elevated consequence.
findings.mitigation: Short-term (before next release): split the release-gate job into two jobs — (1) a gate-evaluation job with permissions {contents: read} only, covering all validation steps including the pip installs; (2) an issue-opening job with permissions {contents: read, issues: write} that runs only on failure() and is triggered via needs: <gate-job>. The issue-opening job requires no pip installs (it uses only gh CLI and a single python3 str.replace() call that can be validated separately). Medium-term: close TF-020H3rg-002 (add pip-compile --generate-hashes for pyyaml + jsonschema in both release-gate.yml and policy-check.yml) — this independently eliminates the PyPI compromise vector in both workflows.

findings.claim: When the Resolve-tag step fails before writing its tag output (e.g., a tag pushed that starts with v but does not match the semver regex), CANDIDATE_TAG is empty in the issue step and the fallback tag="${CANDIDATE_TAG:-${GITHUB_REF##refs/tags/}}" is used without any semver validation. If the raw tag name contains special characters such as a double-quote, the --search "in:title \"${title}\"" argument passed to gh is a malformed GitHub search query, breaking the de-dup check.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml:363-364 — fallback assignment tag="${CANDIDATE_TAG:-${GITHUB_REF##refs/tags/}}" with no subsequent regex gate. release-gate.yml:371 — title="[release-gate-violation] tag ${tag} failed validation": title is assigned via double-quoted bash string; bash does NOT re-evaluate command substitutions that appear in expanded variable values (confirmed by bash word-expansion semantics — parameter expansion and command substitution execute in a single pass left-to-right; a $(…) in the string value of ${tag} is not re-executed). However a literal " in tag causes the GitHub search string passed to gh (line 375-377) to have mismatched inner quotes: in:title "[release-gate-violation] tag v1.0.0" failed validation" — producing an undefined search result and likely an empty existing value, bypassing de-dup. Git ref rules do not forbid " in tag names; GitHub API may or may not enforce additional restrictions. The Resolve-tag step does validate with ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ but exits 1 before setting the tag output, so CANDIDATE_TAG is empty when the issue step fires.
findings.impact: De-dup check bypassed for tags with unusual names: a second run for the same malformed tag would open a duplicate release-gate-violation issue rather than commenting on the existing one. No code execution risk; no shell injection (bash does not re-evaluate variable expansion results). The issue title passed to gh issue create still contains the raw special chars via --title "${title}" which is syntactically safe in bash. Impact is limited to duplicate issues in the SCP tracker.
findings.mitigation: After the fallback assignment, apply the same sanitization as the Resolve-tag step: if ! [[ "${tag}" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then tag="malformed-tag"; fi — or use tag="${tag//[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]/_}" to strip special chars. Either approach preserves the alert (issue is still opened) while ensuring the search query and title are well-formed. Consistent with the Resolve-tag step's existing validation discipline.

findings.claim: gh issue create uses --label release-gate-violation --label needs-triage --label auto-opened but makes no prior assertion that these labels exist in the repository. With set -euo pipefail active, gh CLI returns non-zero for unknown labels, causing the issue step to exit non-zero and silently losing the release-gate-violation alert.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml:456-463 — gh issue create call includes three --label flags with no preceding gh label create or gh api label-existence check. The step has no fallback or error-catching wrapper. Symmetric pattern in canary-replay.yml (which has the same gap) was not flagged in prior reviews because the rule-regression labels are more likely to be set up during initial repo configuration. release-gate-violation is a NEW label introduced by this slice and may not exist on fresh forks or repos set up before this slice landed.
findings.impact: If the labels have not been pre-created (e.g., on a fresh repo, a fork, or after label cleanup), the gh issue create call fails silently. The only visible signal is a failed step in the workflow run (visible in Actions UI) but no GitHub issue is opened and no operator is notified via the issue tracker. The post-tag observer's last-line-of-defense alert is lost entirely, defeating the TF-020H3rg-003 closure intent.
findings.mitigation: Prepend label pre-creation to the step: for each of release-gate-violation, needs-triage, auto-opened, add gh label create "${label}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --force 2>/dev/null || true before the gh issue list de-dup check. The --force flag on gh label create is idempotent (no-ops if the label already exists) and the || true prevents step failure on any label API error. Alternatively document the required labels in a one-time repo-setup step in VERSIONING.md 'Tag-cut procedure' and track with the existing TF mechanism.

findings.claim: The issues:write permission addition has no ratifying D-NNN row in docs/DECISIONS.md, breaking the precedent established by D-029 (which explicitly ratified the statuses:write expansion with threat-surface reasoning). Permission-scope expansions to the release-gate workflow are security-relevant governance events; the D-029 precedent makes a D-NNN row the documented expectation for such changes.
findings.evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md last entry is D-036 (2026-05-01); no entry records the issues:write addition. D-029 (2026-04-29) explicitly ratified the statuses:write expansion with reasoning: 'The statuses:write privilege uses the caller's ${{ github.token }} and posts only to repos/<caller>/statuses/${{ pull_request.head.sha }}; no other write surface is unlocked.' The analogous issues:write reasoning appears only in the workflow comment block (release-gate.yml:66-70) and in the DISPATCH-NOTE.md slice acceptance checklist, neither of which is the canonical decision log. DECISIONS.md is CODEOWNERS-protected (docs/DECISIONS.md @jrnb2024) and serves as the durable audit trail.
findings.impact: Future auditors and estate-cascade adopters cannot trace the issues:write decision to the canonical decision log via the standard D-NNN search pattern. The D-029 precedent implies that permission-scope expansions are governance events warranting their own decision row; omitting one here creates an inconsistency in the audit trail's coverage of privilege-footprint decisions. In single-operator mode this is documentation-only, but as estate scale grows (WP-SCP-024) adopters inspect DECISIONS.md to understand the privilege posture of the workflows they are inheriting.
findings.mitigation: Add a D-037 row to docs/DECISIONS.md in the same PR as or immediately following 020H.3.1: 'D-037 | 2026-05-01 | release-gate.yml permissions block extends to issues:write to support the 020H.3.1 auto-issue step (closes TF-020H3rg-003). Scope: per-repo GITHUB_TOKEN only; fires exclusively on failure() && github.event_name == push; CODEOWNERS-gated workflow change (.github/** @jrnb2024). Threat surface bounded symmetric with D-029 (statuses:write). | ACCEPTED | Minimum-necessary privilege for the last-line-of-defense alarm; no org-wide write surface unlocked.'

findings.claim: The issue-comment body in the de-dup branch uses direct bash string interpolation (--body "Re-detected in workflow run ${RUN_URL}.") while the issue-create body uses Python str.replace() templating. RUN_URL is GitHub-infrastructure-derived and not user-controlled today, so there is no current injection risk, but the pattern inconsistency creates a forward-compatibility trap.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml:382-385 — gh issue comment --body "Re-detected in workflow run ${RUN_URL}." uses direct bash expansion of RUN_URL. release-gate.yml:391-454 — the issue-create body routes through a Python heredoc with explicit str.replace() substitution for CANDIDATE_TAG and RUN_URL, matching the canary-replay.yml fix-round-1 SAFE-MIN-004 pattern closure. RUN_URL is constructed from github.server_url / github.repository / actions/runs / github.run_id — all GitHub-runner-provided values — so no user-controlled injection today. However the comment body path did not exist in canary-replay.yml (which uses --body with multiline heredoc) and is a new pattern introduced by this slice.
findings.impact: If the comment body is extended in a future slice to include a log excerpt, an annotation value from the workflow output, or any other user-influenced string, the direct-expansion pattern will be inherited without a visible safety signal. The asymmetry with the issue-create body is also a maintenance trap: a developer reading the step may assume both bodies are equivalent in safety posture.
findings.mitigation: Route the comment body through Python templating for consistency: body_comment=$(python3 -c 'import os; print("Re-detected in workflow run " + os.environ.get("RUN_URL", "<unknown>") + ".")') then gh issue comment --body "${body_comment}". Or use printf '%s' as the delimiter-safe alternative. One-liner, no structural change to the step.

self_reported_concerns: SAFE-MAJ-001 represents a real privilege amplification introduced by this slice — the two-step exploit chain (PyPI compromise + unverified pip install + new issues:write scope) was not present before 020H.3.1. It does not constitute a blocker for merge in the current single-operator threat model (only @jrnb2024 can push tags or merge PRs), but it should be addressed before TF-020H3rg-002 goes stale long enough that the supply-chain gap becomes operationally relevant for an estate-cascade deployment.
structured_review.summary: SAFETY/BYPASS lens R1 on commit 1a12f68. The auto-issue step's primary threat model is adversarial analysis of six surfaces: (1) issues:write privilege scope — per-repo GITHUB_TOKEN, CODEOWNERS-gated workflow, bounded; sound but over-broad at job level relative to minimum-necessary; (2) failure()&&push gate — correctly excludes workflow_dispatch, no cron on release-gate.yml, no release: event; sound; (3) malicious-tag-push trigger — tag-push requires repo write (only @jrnb2024); new-tag creation allowed by D-030 rulesets but alert assignment routes to operator; blast radius bounded; sound; (4) de-dup search injection — CANDIDATE_TAG regex-validated and safe; GITHUB_REF fallback (when Resolve-tag fails before setting output) bypasses validation and could malform the GitHub search query with special-char tag names; de-dup failure risk only, no code execution (bash does not re-evaluate command substitutions from variable expansion); (5) Python heredoc + str.replace() body construction — safe; (6) gh issue create --body "${body}" — safe. Five findings: 1 MAJ, 3 MIN, 1 nit.
structured_review.verdict_rationale: No CRIT findings. One MAJ finding (issues:write granted at job level amplifies the existing unverified-pip-install risk from TF-020H3rg-002 into a two-step supply-chain exploit chain — fixable by job-split or TF-020H3rg-002 closure). Three MIN findings (GITHUB_REF fallback bypasses semver sanitization in the de-dup search path; label pre-existence assumed with silent alert loss; no D-NNN ratifying the issues:write permission expansion per the D-029 precedent). One nit (comment-body direct bash expansion inconsistent with issue-create body's Python templating). All findings are fixable without altering the slice's observable contract or descoping any AC. The core bypass and injection surfaces (failure() gate, GITHUB_REF injection, Python str.replace(), CODEOWNERS coverage, tag-protection D-030) are sound.
